two-pointers.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
two-pointers.note: The canonical converging two-pointer problem — sorted input is the tell.

two-pointers.title: Valid Palindrome
two-pointers.note: Pointers converge from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters.

two-pointers.title: Container With Most Water
two-pointers.note: Greedy two pointers: always move the shorter wall inward.

two-pointers.title: 3Sum
two-pointers.note: Fix one pointer, two-pointer sweep the rest — sort first.

two-pointers.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
two-pointers.note: Fast/slow pointers moving in the same direction (in-place compaction).

two-pointers.title: Trapping Rain Water
two-pointers.note: Two pointers tracking running max height from both sides.

sliding-window.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
sliding-window.note: A window of size 1 that tracks the running minimum — the simplest window.

sliding-window.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
sliding-window.note: Classic variable-size window with a hash set tracking window contents.

sliding-window.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
sliding-window.note: Shrink-while-valid pattern — grow right, shrink left once the sum condition holds.

sliding-window.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
sliding-window.note: Window is valid as long as (window size - count of most frequent char) <= k.

sliding-window.title: Sliding Window Maximum
sliding-window.note: Monotonic deque inside a fixed window — the hard-mode version of this pattern.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Linked List Cycle
fast-slow-pointers.note: The canonical Floyd's cycle detection — if fast ever equals slow, there's a loop.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Middle of the Linked List
fast-slow-pointers.note: Slow lands on the middle exactly when fast (moving 2x) reaches the end.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Linked List Cycle II
fast-slow-pointers.note: Detect the cycle, then reset one pointer to head — they meet at the cycle's start.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Happy Number
fast-slow-pointers.note: No linked list at all — the 'next' function is digit-square-sum, but the cycle-detection trick still applies.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Palindrome Linked List
fast-slow-pointers.note: Fast/slow finds the middle in one pass, then reverse the second half and compare.

fast-slow-pointers.title: Find the Duplicate Number
fast-slow-pointers.note: Treat array values as 'next' pointers — a duplicate value forces a cycle to exist.

monotonic-stack.title: Next Greater Element I
monotonic-stack.note: The textbook warm-up — build the next-greater map with a single decreasing stack pass.

monotonic-stack.title: Daily Temperatures
monotonic-stack.note: Same next-greater idea, but the stack stores indices so you can compute a distance.

monotonic-stack.title: Next Greater Element II
monotonic-stack.note: Circular array variant — iterate 2n times, indexing with i % n.

monotonic-stack.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
monotonic-stack.note: A monotonic increasing stack of bar indices — popping resolves the rectangle's right boundary.

monotonic-stack.title: Trapping Rain Water
monotonic-stack.note: A decreasing stack of walls — popping resolves a trapped-water 'bucket' between two taller bars.

monotonic-stack.title: Remove K Digits
monotonic-stack.note: Greedily pop larger digits off an increasing stack to build the smallest possible number.

tree-bfs.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
tree-bfs.note: The textbook version — queue, track level size, drain one level at a time.

tree-bfs.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
tree-bfs.note: Same level-order skeleton, aggregate per level instead of collecting nodes.

tree-bfs.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
tree-bfs.note: BFS finds the shallowest leaf in O(n) without exploring the whole tree — beats DFS here.

tree-bfs.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
tree-bfs.note: Level order with a direction flip every other level.

tree-bfs.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
tree-bfs.note: Level order traversal, keep only the last node visited per level.

tree-bfs.title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
tree-bfs.note: Level order traversal while linking siblings as you drain the queue.

merge-intervals.title: Merge Intervals
merge-intervals.note: The canonical version — sort by start, sweep, merge overlapping runs.

merge-intervals.title: Insert Interval
merge-intervals.note: Same merge logic, but you're inserting one new interval into an already-sorted, already-merged list.

merge-intervals.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
merge-intervals.note: Sort by end time instead of start — greedily keep the interval that ends soonest.

merge-intervals.title: Meeting Rooms II
merge-intervals.note: Track concurrent overlap count with a min-heap of end times, or a start/end sweep line.

merge-intervals.title: Interval List Intersections
merge-intervals.note: Two-pointer sweep across two already-sorted interval lists, emitting overlap ranges.

merge-intervals.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
merge-intervals.note: Sort by end coordinate — a variant of the greedy non-overlapping-intervals idea.

top-k-elements.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
top-k-elements.note: The textbook warm-up — a size-k min-heap gives you the kth largest directly at the root.

top-k-elements.title: Top K Frequent Elements
top-k-elements.note: Count frequencies first, then run the same size-k min-heap pattern over the counts.

top-k-elements.title: K Closest Points to Origin
top-k-elements.note: Same pattern with a max-heap of size k keyed on distance instead of raw value.

top-k-elements.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
top-k-elements.note: A twist on top-K — a min-heap seeded with each row's first element, popped k times.

top-k-elements.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
top-k-elements.note: Heap holds candidate pairs instead of raw numbers — same size-k pruning idea.

top-k-elements.title: Task Scheduler
top-k-elements.note: Greedy scheduling driven by a max-heap of remaining task frequencies.

modified-binary-search.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
modified-binary-search.note: The canonical version — figure out which half is sorted, then decide where the target could be.

modified-binary-search.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
modified-binary-search.note: Duplicates can make both halves look 'sorted' — when nums[lo] === nums[mid] === nums[hi], shrink the window by one from each side instead.

modified-binary-search.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
modified-binary-search.note: No target to find — just locate the rotation point by comparing mid against the right edge.

modified-binary-search.title: Find Peak Element
modified-binary-search.note: Binary search on a condition (uphill vs downhill slope) rather than on sorted order directly.

modified-binary-search.title: Koko Eating Bananas
modified-binary-search.note: Binary search over the answer space itself — search for the smallest eating speed that satisfies a feasibility check.

subsets.title: Subsets
subsets.note: The exact include/exclude recursion tree visualized above.

subsets.title: Subsets II
subsets.note: Duplicates in the input need a sort-first + skip-same-sibling rule to avoid duplicate subsets.

subsets.title: Permutations
subsets.note: Same backtracking shape, but the branching factor is 'which unused element goes next' instead of include/exclude.

subsets.title: Combination Sum
subsets.note: Adds real pruning — abandon a branch the moment the running sum exceeds the target.

subsets.title: Palindrome Partitioning
subsets.note: The 'choice' at each step is where to cut next, constrained by the palindrome check as the pruning rule.

bit-manipulation.title: Single Number
bit-manipulation.note: The canonical XOR-cancellation problem — exactly the demo visualized above.

bit-manipulation.title: Number of 1 Bits
bit-manipulation.note: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit — count how many times you can do that.

bit-manipulation.title: Counting Bits
bit-manipulation.note: DP built on a bit trick: bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1) — reuse smaller answers instead of recomputing popcount.

bit-manipulation.title: Reverse Bits
bit-manipulation.note: Shift-and-mask each bit into its mirrored position, 32 times.

bit-manipulation.title: Single Number II
bit-manipulation.note: Every number appears three times except one — plain XOR isn't enough; track bit counts mod 3 instead.

bit-manipulation.title: Sum of Two Integers
bit-manipulation.note: Add two integers without + or - : XOR gives the sum-without-carry, AND-then-shift gives the carry, repeat until no carry remains.

two-heaps.title: Find Median from Data Stream
two-heaps.note: The textbook two-heaps problem — exactly the running-median demo visualized above.

two-heaps.title: Sliding Window Median
two-heaps.note: Two heaps plus lazy deletion — entries leaving the window are marked stale instead of removed immediately.

two-heaps.title: IPO
two-heaps.note: A max-heap of affordable projects by profit, refilled from a min-heap of projects sorted by required capital.

two-heaps.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
two-heaps.note: A single size-k min-heap — a good warm-up before combining two heaps for a full running median.

two-heaps.title: Find Right Interval
two-heaps.note: Pair a heap of interval start times with a heap of end times to match each interval to its nearest right neighbor.

cyclic-sort.title: Missing Number
cyclic-sort.note: Cyclic-sort the array of 0..n, then the first index that doesn't hold its own value reveals the gap.

cyclic-sort.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
cyclic-sort.note: After a cyclic sort pass, every index not holding value (index + 1) names a missing number.

cyclic-sort.title: Find the Duplicate Number
cyclic-sort.note: A cyclic-sort pass finds it directly — the swap loop stalls the instant it hits a value already in its target slot.

cyclic-sort.title: Set Mismatch
cyclic-sort.note: One cyclic sort pass exposes both the duplicate (the value already sitting at its own index) and the missing number (the index left unfilled).

cyclic-sort.title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
cyclic-sort.note: Same swap-to-home-index loop as Missing Number — duplicates are whatever's still stuck out of place afterward.

cyclic-sort.title: First Missing Positive
cyclic-sort.note: Cyclic sort every in-range positive into its slot in O(n)/O(1), then scan once for the first index that doesn't match.

k-way-merge.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
k-way-merge.note: The k=2 base case — understand this before generalizing to k lists with a heap.

k-way-merge.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
k-way-merge.note: The canonical k-way merge — a size-k min-heap of list heads, exactly the demo visualized above.

k-way-merge.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
k-way-merge.note: Each matrix row is already a sorted list — k-way merge the rows and stop after popping the kth element.

k-way-merge.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
k-way-merge.note: Treat 'nums1[i] + nums2[j] for fixed i' as one sorted list per i — merge them with a heap instead of generating every pair.

k-way-merge.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
k-way-merge.note: K-way merge with a twist — track the current max alongside the heap's min to shrink the covering range as you go.
